correctness.rationale: Fourier–Plancherel on the longitudinal Z variable yields the exact fiber M_t(ω)=[[1,0],[q cosh(t/3),q sinh(t/3)]] for q=e^{-t(1−2cosω/3)}, bounded away from zero for each fixed t>0. Its Gram form is diag(1,0)+q² vv*, nondecreasing in q², so the sharp essential lower endpoint is ω=π and upper endpoint ω=0. Putting r=e^{-2t/3} gives M_-=[[1,0],[r²(1+r)/2,r²(1−r)/2]], M_+=[[1,0],[(1+r)/2,(1−r)/2]], hence exact traces and determinants and both quadratic eigenvalue bounds. Fourier inversion gives the bounded explicit recovery formula for f_1. Differentiating the lower characteristic root gives critical polynomial P=3r^6−3r^5+5r^4−5r^3+5r²+4r−4; its stated derivative decomposition is strictly positive on [0,1]. P(0)<0<P(2/3), critical eigenvalue lies on the small branch, and the boundary lower bound tends to zero at both ends, proving a unique global optimum. Independently verified the polynomial resultant identity exactly using SymPy and r*=0.6377325420915736, t*=0.6747544448314551, A*=0.004882704478092798.

value.rationale: Observing only one entire rail at two times is a concrete natural undersampling design. The sharp worst-case recovery energy, explicit inverse and unique delay maximizing the lower frame bound provide an optimal robustness parameter for every ℓ² input. It is not just sampling injectivity, a generic Vandermonde criterion, or an arbitrary scalar optimization; the physically meaningful worst-case stability objective and full continuous spectral extremum are resolved.

limitations: ℓ²(Z)^2, full spatial coverage of one rail, normalized unweighted degree-three graph Laplacian, exactly t=0 and one later time; not noisy missing spatial samples.
Exact finite-cycle tests are corroborative; the fiber and derivative proof establishes the infinite-system theorem.
